why: TANITAD_PROGRAMME.md §5 charter: 'Criteria completeness is enforced by machinery, not memory — we measurably failed to keep them complete by hand.' This file is the machine-readable registry every eval output is diffed against. A criterion may be PRESENT or REFUSED-with-a-reason; it may never be SILENTLY ABSENT.

three_states.PRESENT: the metric is in the artifact at one of its keys
three_states.REFUSED: the artifact's `refused` block names the criterion AND gives a reason — admissible, and becomes a WORK ITEM
three_states.ABSENT: neither — VIOLATION. This is the silent omission the doctrine forbids.

doctrine.families_never_pooled: The four families are reported per-family. A single composite hides the trade-off we are trying to see.
doctrine.ade_alone_is_incomplete: ADE stays, but an eval reporting ADE alone must not be presented as a result (PI, 2026-08-02, binding).
doctrine.estimator: paired episode-cluster bootstrap over val episodes (taniteval/ci.py)
doctrine.forbidden_estimator: overlapping_holdout_se — biases the point estimate bidirectionally, up to a sign flip
doctrine.tier_required: every artifact carries its tier; T0 is a WM diagnostic and is NEVER driving performance

applicability.why: A criteria check that scores PROFILING artifacts against DRIVING criteria reports a huge violation count that is pure noise — and a probe reporting the wrong scope is worse than no probe (the `df` trap, the Thor `free` trap, the cgroup `usage_in_bytes` trap). Scope is therefore decided BEFORE any criterion is evaluated, and an artifact whose kind cannot be determined is reported as UNKNOWN, never silently dropped and never counted as compliant.

out_of_scope_if_any.reason: corpus census artifact, not an eval
clip-level dump, not a scored eval

T0.note: teacher-forced world-model fidelity diagnostic. NEVER reported as driving performance.

T1.note: action-closed loop — the PRIMARY driving tier.

LONGITUDINAL.why: 88.7 % of our oracle gap is longitudinal. ADE hides it — an arm can win ADE while setting the wrong speed.

criteria.label: target-speed accuracy
criteria.note: MAE and signed bias; the bias is what exposes systematic over-prediction.

criteria.label: distance-keeping (headway / time-gap / TTC to the lead agent)
criteria.note: MEASURED 2026-08-23: refused in 27/27 complete artifacts — 'no lead-agent state exists (lead_state is a None stub)'. Largest open criterion gap, on the family owning most of the oracle gap.

LATERAL.why: 'lateral is fine' has been asserted from cross-track alone; curvature and yaw are where a smooth-but-wrong path shows up.

criteria.label: curvature error
criteria.note: MEASURED 2026-08-23: magnitude refused in 27/27 ('measured 24x the signal; SIGN agreement only at tier 0'). curv_sign_agree is a PARTIAL satisfaction — sign without magnitude.

criteria.label: yaw-rate error
criteria.note: MEASURED 2026-08-23: ABSENT in 71/71 artifacts and NOT in any refused block — a silent omission.

TACTICAL.why: The 5-way manoeuvre softmax that MIXES lat+lon is our single largest known defect; a scalar ADE cannot see a decision error.

criteria.label: manoeuvre-decision quality (selected vs executed)
criteria.note: MEASURED 2026-08-23: ABSENT in 71/71 and NOT refused — silent omission.

criteria.label: confusion over the manoeuvre classes
criteria.note: MEASURED 2026-08-23: the emitter writes `confusion_gt_rows_pred_cols` (four_families.py:563), together with `per_class` recall/precision and `never_predicted`. An earlier registry looked for `confusion` and the census duly reported '0/135, silently absent everywhere' - a REGISTRY TYPO wearing a finding's clothes. See C133-b. `never_predicted` is the load-bearing field: the deployed arm emitted 0 of 881 'accelerate' decisions, which no accuracy scalar can show.

STRATEGIC.why: The hierarchy is the programme's thesis. If we never measure the strategic level we cannot claim it works.

criteria.label: strategic decision quality
criteria.note: MEASURED 2026-08-23: ABSENT in 71/71 and NOT refused — silent omission.

criteria.label: strategic route / goal-setting quality
criteria.note: A route head that is a bijection of its own nav input scores 1.0000 by ECHO, not skill (MEASURED 2026-08-03, flagship v1: 369/369 and 81/81). Any route/goal score must ship its echo test.

leak_guards.why: For ANY head, ask whether its inputs at inference include something the label was derived from. Same family as the C6 confound and the REF-A I-JEPA leak (~80 % of val inside train).

guards.rule: Inference uses VISION ONLY. Labels may use ego/privileged data (PI, 2026-08-03, binding).
guards.note: An artifact must state what the model consumed at inference, or its number cannot be checked for this.

guards.rule: The goal path and the situation path stay information-disjoint at inference; a goal input must not carry the situation classifier's output in any form (PI, 2026-08-03, binding).
A route/goal head scoring near 1.0 must publish its echo test against its own input.

criteria.label: tier stamp present
criteria.note: MEASURED 2026-08-23: only 27/71 artifacts carry any tier marker.

criteria.label: overlapping_holdout_se not used as a decision-grade interval
criteria.note: It may appear ONLY under an explicitly deprecated label, or in the `deprecated_and_refused` field.

criteria.label: corpus identity recorded (parity key + skip-hash)
criteria.note: Parity is sacred: the canonical train corpus is `physicalai-train-e438721ae894` (2376 episodes), skip-hash `f09e44db`. An artifact that does not record WHICH corpus it scored is not cross-arm comparable, and every delta computed against it is uninterpretable. Anything that re-selects episodes must be flagged NON-PARITY explicitly.

criteria.label: headline metrics reported against their trivial control(s)
criteria.note: ⭐ THE CRITERION THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THE PROGRAMME'S LARGEST MISREAD. A model number without its control is unreadable: MEASURED 2026-08-23, the T1 `stage-a-repaired · cl` arm reads 9.3697 m while its own hold-action control reads 0.4246 m on the SAME windows — the trivial baseline beat the model 22×. An artifact reporting only the model's value looks like a result. Controls: hold-v0 (go straight at the observed entry speed) and constant velocity. ⛔ A paired interval that excludes zero while favouring the FLOOR means the trivial baseline won — render that as LOST, never as a tie.

benchmarks._status: FILLED 2026-08-23 from the banked protocol specs. A benchmark is enforced only for an artifact that CLAIMS it (a `benchmark` key). Adopting a benchmark means running ITS published protocol verbatim and citing it - never ours relabelled.
benchmarks._four_families_still_bind: An EPDMS or an L2 number does NOT satisfy the four-families rule. Tactical and strategic are absent from NavSim BY CONSTRUCTION, as are longitudinal target-speed and lateral heading/curvature/yaw. A benchmark artifact must REFUSE each absent family explicitly, with its reason and n.

navsim.THE_COLUMN_TRAP: READ `score`, NEVER `pdm_score`. PDMScorer._aggregate_pdm_scores masks Extended Comfort out and divides by 14; the real EPDMS (denominator 16) is assembled downstream in run_pdm_score.py::compute_final_scores. The wrong column looks perfectly valid.
navsim.ESTIMATOR_UNRESOLVED: Our episode-cluster bootstrap does NOT transfer - NavSim's resampling unit is a scene token, not an episode. Do not report a NavSim CI until the cluster unit is settled and pre-registered.

PDMS_v1.note: DDC exists in v1 code with weight 0.0 (pdm_scorer.py:39-48)

criteria.label: EPDMS/PDMS from the `score` column
criteria.note: NOT `pdm_score` - see the column trap above.

criteria.label: which variant + split named
criteria.note: PDMS_v1 vs EPDMS_v2, and navtest vs navhard. 'EPDMS on navtest' (64-87) is NOT navhard EPDMS (11-55); four incomparable protocols exist.

criteria.label: every sub-metric reported
criteria.note: A composite alone hides which term moved.

criteria.label: declared ego inputs (vision-only compliance)
criteria.note: NavSim publishes NO fully ego-free number; even 'camera-only' LTF consumes driving_command + ego_velocity + ego_acceleration. Design against TransFuser B1 'Goal only' = 81.8 PDMS. driving_command is 4-dim in the devkit, not the 3 the paper states.

criteria.label: route_roadblock_ids provenance checked
criteria.note: UNVERIFIED whether nuPlan's route_roadblock_ids derives from the expert path. Run this leak check BEFORE quoting a route-conditioned result - same family as our route-head echo.

GATE_estimator_cluster_unit.rule: A NavSim artifact MUST declare `estimator.cluster_unit`. Until the unit is settled and PRE-REGISTERED, the only admissible interval is an explicit {status:UNAVAILABLE, reason, n}. ⛔ A bare point estimate with no interval block, or an interval computed with the episode-cluster bootstrap, FAILS.
GATE_estimator_cluster_unit.why: Our episode-cluster bootstrap does not transfer: NavSim resamples SCENE TOKENS, not episodes, and NavSim scenes are explicitly allowed to OVERLAP (PUB-DEVKIT docs/splits.md: 'NavSim splits contain overlapping scenes'). Resampling overlapping units as if independent understates the variance — the same family as overlapping_holdout_se, which biases the POINT ESTIMATE bidirectionally up to a sign flip. Inventing a CI here would reproduce a retracted defect on a borrowed benchmark.
GATE_estimator_cluster_unit.admissible_until_settled: UNAVAILABLE with a reason and n

GATE_ego_status_enforcement.rule: A NavSim artifact MUST carry `protocol.ego_status_enforcement` naming the MECHANISM by which the agent did not read ego status, and the evidence for it. ⛔ 'we did not use it' is an assertion, not enforcement, and FAILS.
GATE_ego_status_enforcement.why: MEASURED from the devkit: there is NO switch that removes ego status. `EgoStatus` (ego_velocity, ego_acceleration, ego_pose) is ALWAYS populated on AgentInput and nothing in the framework verifies an agent declined to read it — `SensorConfig` gates cameras and LiDAR only. Our vision-only rule (PI, 2026-08-03, binding) is therefore ours alone to enforce and evidence. This is the leak-guard question in a borrowed harness: an input that is present at inference is consumed unless something PREVENTS it.
acceptable_mechanisms: the agent never receives EgoStatus (zeroed/stripped at the adapter seam, asserted in a test)
an ablation showing the metric is unchanged when ego fields are randomised

GATE_modality_label.rule: A NavSim artifact MUST declare `protocol.sensor_set` and `protocol.setting` (e.g. 'front-camera-only, perception-free'). ⛔ Comparing our row against a multi-camera or perception-based row without both fields present FAILS.
GATE_modality_label.why: The leaderboard server records NO modality — only TEAM_NAME, AUTHORS, EMAIL, INSTITUTION, COUNTRY — so every 'camera-only' claim in the field is the authors', not the server's. MEASURED 2026-08-27 from the banked primary: Drive-JEPA's 93.7 PDMS headline uses 1024x256 stacking FRONT+LEFT+RIGHT, while its perception-free row uses the front camera only at 512x256. Comparing our single 256x640 front-camera arm against the 93.7 row would be a category error in our own favour's opposite direction — and comparing it against the perception-free ladder is legitimate. The label is what makes the difference visible.

comparable_ladder_perception_free_front_._source: PUB-PAPER Drive-JEPA (arXiv 2601.22032) Table 1, read from the banked PDF
comparable_ladder_perception_free_front_._note: This is TanitAD's comparable class: front-camera-only, perception-free (supervised solely by human trajectories, no perception annotations), entry rung 21M and top rung 307M — our scale band.

published_reference_numbers._evidence: PUB-PAPER, extracted by the EvalFlyWheel from the banked PDFs 2026-08-27
published_reference_numbers.drive_jepa_v1_PDMS_NOTE: ⛔ 93.7, NOT 93.3. The abstract and §1 both say 93.7; the 93.3 appears only in the paper's own NeurIPS checklist, where it misquotes its own abstract. Cite 93.7 and note the internal inconsistency if the figure is load-bearing.
published_reference_numbers._harness_pin: ⛔ v1 PDMS must come from the v1.1 BRANCH — `main` is v2 and its scorer is the EPDMS scorer, so 'v1 PDMS from main' silently computes a different metric. Neither paper states a devkit SHA, and the 2025-09-29 human-filter bugfix (issue #151) sits between v2.2 and now, so which side they are on is UNVERIFIED. Pin OUR SHA beside our number.

nuscenes.licence_status: CONFLICT, UNRESOLVED: the paper states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial); the AWS Open Data registry lists 'Commercial'. Treat as RESEARCH-ONLY until written terms are obtained.

planning_openloop.THE_VERDICT: INADMISSIBLE as a TanitAD criterion or gate. Usable ONLY as a cited external-comparability row. Three measurements: (1) the averaging convention alone moves one VAD checkpoint 0.72 -> 1.22 m (+70 %) and FLIPS the UniAD/VAD ranking; (2) the ground-truth HUMAN trajectory scores 0.36-0.96 % collision - the metric's false-positive floor exceeds the published spread; (3) AD-MLP with no camera and no LiDAR ties a full perception stack. And VAD's 'high-level command' is computed from the GT future trajectory thresholded at +/-2 m and handed back as an input - OUR route-head echo defect, published as state of the art.

criteria.label: which evaluation implementation produced the number
criteria.note: uniad (L2 AT the timestep) vs stp3 (L2 averaged UP TO it). Five axes of divergence, not one. An untagged L2 is not comparable to anything.

criteria.label: the GT-trajectory control published alongside
criteria.note: The echo test applied to a borrowed instrument: report what the ground-truth human trajectory scores under the same protocol. Without it the number cannot be read.

criteria.label: high-level command refused, or replaced by a predicted goal
criteria.note: The GT-derived command is inadmissible under our vision-only rule.

criteria.label: the non-straight subset reported alongside full val
criteria.note: Most of nuScenes val is straight-line constant-velocity driving.

schema_note: Two artifact schemas are recognised: `taniteval.driving` (headline.* + a top-level `refused` block) and `four_families` (ff_*.json, per-family blocks whose criteria decline inline via {status:UNAVAILABLE, reason, n}). Both refusal idioms are honest and both are read.

registry_hygiene.why: A criterion whose keys resolve in NO artifact anywhere is far more likely a REGISTRY TYPO than a universal absence. This happened twice on 2026-08-23 (tac.confusion), and the second time it was published to the PI as 'the surviving universal gap'. The checker therefore reports UNRESOLVABLE separately from ABSENT, and a test pins that every criterion resolves in at least one real artifact.
registry_hygiene.rule: Adding a criterion means naming the key the EMITTER actually writes. Read the producing code, do not guess the name. If a metric is genuinely not emitted anywhere yet, set `not_yet_emitted: true` so the intent is explicit and the audit stays green.

release_gate.why: The PI asked (2026-08-23) to finalize the tests and criteria that must run at EVERY model release. This block names which registry criteria are release-blocking, so the gate and the census read one source.
blocking: all four families PRESENT or REFUSED-with-reason-and-n
release_gate.blocking_note: Each is cheap, objective, and earned by a measured failure. ⛔ A T1 artifact is REQUIRED: T0 is a world-model diagnostic and a release may never be gated on it alone.
advisory: regression vs the previous release (per family)
release_gate.advisory_note: Advisory until two clean releases exist to compare — a regression gate with no trustworthy baseline manufactures false failures.
release_gate.cannot_rule_is_a_verdict: ⭐ A criterion that cannot decide at the configured settings must return CANNOT-RULE, loudly — never a silent PASS and never a perpetual INCONCLUSIVE. MEASURED precedent: the O6 rank gate could never rule (spectrum n=24 against a ceiling of 1024) and its silence was read as a pass for weeks.
release_gate.pi_decision_open: Whether a FAIL blocks the release or advises is the PI's call (open as of 2026-08-23). Recommendation on record: blocking on the list above, advisory on regression.
